title: Practice Pack: Work and Energy
subject: Science
chapter: Topic-based: use with whichever Class 9 book your students follow
instructions: Level 1 checks the ideas, Level 2 is board-style numericals, and Level 3 is Foundation-level challenge.
Key relations: W = F × s · KE = ½mv^{2} · PE = mgh · P = W/t · 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10^{6} J
Use the value of g given in each question.

questions.q: Define work and give its SI unit.
questions.answer: Work is done when a force moves an object in the direction of the force: W = F × s. The SI unit is the joule (J). 1 J = 1 N × 1 m.

questions.q: Give two situations where a force acts but no work is done.
questions.answer: (1) Pushing a wall that does not move (no displacement). (2) Carrying a load on your head while walking on level ground: the force of gravity is perpendicular to the displacement, so gravity does no work.

questions.q: Define power and give its SI unit.
questions.answer: Power is the rate of doing work (P = W/t). The SI unit is the watt (W) = 1 J/s.

questions.q: State the law of conservation of energy.
questions.answer: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed. It can only change from one form to another, so the total energy stays the same.

questions.q: How many joules are there in 1 kWh?
A force of 7 N moves an object 8 m in the direction of the force. How much work is done?
Find the kinetic energy of a 15 kg object moving at 4 m/s.
Find the potential energy of a 10 kg object at a height of 6 m. (g = 9.8 m/s^{2})
A lamp uses 1000 J of electrical energy in 10 s. What is its power?
How much work is needed to increase the speed of a 1500 kg car from 30 km/h to 60 km/h?
A 1500 W heater runs for 10 hours. How much energy does it use, in kWh?
questions.answer: E = P × t = 1.5 kW × 10 h = 15 kWh.

questions.q: Two girls, each weighing 400 N, climb a rope to a height of 8 m. Girl A takes 20 s and girl B takes 50 s. Find the power of each.
questions.answer: Work by each = 400 × 8 = 3200 J. Power of A = 3200/20 = 160 W. Power of B = 3200/50 = 64 W.

questions.q: A boy of mass 50 kg runs up a staircase of 45 steps in 9 s. Each step is 15 cm high. Find his power. (g = 10 m/s^{2})
An object of mass 40 kg is raised to a height of 5 m. Find its potential energy. If it is allowed to fall, find its kinetic energy when it is halfway down. (g = 10 m/s^{2})
questions.answer: PE = mgh = 40 × 10 × 5 = 2000 J. Halfway down, PE = 40 × 10 × 2.5 = 1000 J. By conservation of energy, KE = 2000 – 1000 = 1000 J.

closing: Energy is never lost, only changed. Use that idea to check your answers!
